transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-14 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Mina (Redwood SE), Priya (BrightLayer Head of ML), Tom (Infra Lead), Raj (Product)
-- Optional summary (auto-gen may be noisy) --
Summary: Align on POC acceptance tests: pass/fail thresholds for latency/throughput/error, quality acceptance (label F1/accuracy), reporting format (CSV + dashboard) and timeline for signoff. Action owners and next steps captured.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roundtable — who we got?
[00:06] Priya: Priya here, hi. Head of ML at BrightLayer. We're leading the use-case for summarization + triage of patient messages.
[00:11] Tom: Tom — infra, will own the env and network.
[00:13] Raj: Raj here for product, mainly success metrics and deployment gating.
[00:17] Jordan: Great. Mina, want to kick off with proposed pass/fail matrix?
[00:20] Mina: Sure. I shared a working spreadsheet, POC_benchmarks.xlsx, in the calendar — apologies if the link was weird in the invite. High level: we propose pass/fail across three axes: reliability (error rates/99th pct), performance (p50/p95 latency, throughput at target concurrency), and quality (task-specific metric: labeled accuracy/F1 on your eval set). Also an overall tie-breaker score.
[00:40] Priya: Cool. For quality, we need to be strict — if summaries flip critical PHI fields or mis-triage, that's a fail. We have an internal taxonomy with severity tags.
[00:51] Mina: Understood. For numbers we propose: quality acceptance = weighted F1 >= 0.78 on the canonical set of 300 dev examples; latency p95 < 1.2s for single-request 1k-token-ish chats; throughput sustain of 60 qps for batched async arrivals with 150 concurrent clients (this maps to your traffic profile, Jordan referenced your provided sample). Error rate — request error < 0.5% and model fallback correctness within 2% of baseline.
[01:20] Raj: The 60 qps number seems high, can you show how you mapped our traffic?
[01:25] Mina: Yeah, we used the 24-hour profile you shared in the earlier mail — roughly 30% peak, and the idea is P95 of peak sustained windows. We should double-check the arrival shape though.
[01:33] Tom: Quick security question — for the test runs do we need Redwood Dedicated or can hosted suffice? We need to test key rotation and KMS integration.
[01:41] Jordan: Good point. For acceptance we typically run benchmarks on a dedicated environment that matches the customer's final environment. For security integrations we can run the test in your VPC with Redwood Private (customer-managed KMS) or a dedicated Redwood pool that we configure with your KMS keys. It's a little different depending on whether you require on-prem strictness.
[02:00] Priya: We prefer VPC with our KMS, that's mandatory for the PII workload.
[02:04] Mina: Noted. We'll scope that in the runbook. For the pass/fail matrix doc we have a column for "env": hosted/dedicated/vpc — we'll mark POC target as VPC.

[02:20] Mina: Back to quality metrics: we propose two levels — functional acceptance and safety acceptance. Functional is F1 >= 0.78 and average Rouge-L >= 0.45 on the dev set. Safety: zero critical privacy extraction errors in 300 examples and <=5 minor privacy flags. We'll instrument with our safety hooks and capture examples.
[02:42] Priya: Can we break out exact match and a manual review bucket? We want to human-review 50 failed cases sample.
[02:48] Mina: Yes, we'll export a failure CSV with labels, model output, context, and a link to the trace. Format will be CSV + a dashboard snapshot (Redwood Console link).

[03:00] Jordan: On benchmarks, Mina, what will you run? SDK? TF?
[03:03] Mina: We'll provide a benchmark script that hits the same API as production — Node and Python examples. It will exercise your canonical prompts, with warm KV cache and cold runs. We'll run three replicates per config. Output CSV will include timestamp, model variant, quantization tag, concurrency, batch size, token counts, p50/p95 latencies, token/sec, error counts, and perf counters.
[03:25] Tom: Will the KV caching behavior be realistic? Our live traffic has a lot of prefix reuse.
[03:30] Mina: We'll seed the cache with your prefix distribution. Please include a representative sample when you send the traffic profile.

[03:40] Raj: What's the go/no-go decision logic? If quality is 0.77 (just under) but latency is great, do we call it fail?
[03:47] Jordan: We usually use the pass/fail table plus a scoring rubric — primary gating is safety and quality. If quality misses by a hair, we propose an exception path: run a short remediation — tweak prompts, model variant, or quantization — and re-run within 72 hours. If still below, that's a fail.
[04:03] Priya: That sounds sensible, but we need the short clock and documentation of changes.
[04:07] Mina: We'll record each remediation step in the benchmark report and mark timestamps and config diffs. The report will include a delta analysis comparing baseline to remediation.

[04:20] [crosstalk] Tom: Also, how will we measure hallucination risk? We have internal heuristics.
[04:26] Mina: We'll instrument a hallucination score using your labelled set — and surface examples. If hallucination rate > 5% on high-severity items it's a fail.

[04:38] Priya: Can you also include per-entity precision/recall for PHI types? That matters for compliance.
[04:44] Mina: Yep, we'll add entity-level metrics for PHI detection.

[04:50] Jordan: One practical question — what's the reporting format and cadence?
[04:53] Mina: Primary deliverable: CSV export plus a Redwood Console snapshot and a short PDF executive summary. We'll hand over a single, time-stamped folder with: raw CSVs, a replay script, remediation diffs, and a dashboard link. We'll do a mid-POC checkpoint after the first benchmark run (approx day 7) and final acceptance report at POC close.
[05:14] Raj: How is the dashboard interactive? Can Product filter by severity and by prompt cluster?
[05:19] Mina: Yes, the Console allows filtering by tag, prompt cluster, model variant, and time. We'll also provide a static CSV if you want to put into your own analytics.

[05:30] Tom: Network constraints — we'll need to validate egress and IP allowlist. Mina, can you list the egress IPs or do we need to do a VPC peering?
[05:38] Mina: For VPC mode we'll set up peering or a private link — we'll include the runbook with ports and IP ranges. For testing we can temporarily open an allowlist for our runner. We'll include steps in the runbook.

[05:50] Priya: Timeline — what's realistic to get to acceptance?
[05:53] Jordan: Proposed schedule: Week 0 (this week): agree pass/fail matrix + send eval set. Week 1: Redwood builds runbook + benchmark script; run initial benchmark. Week 2: remediation and second run. Week 3: final report and sign-off. So roughly 3 weeks if inputs are timely.
[06:10] Priya: We can commit to deliver eval set and traffic profile by 2025-07-21. That locks to a final report by mid-August?
[06:18] Jordan: Yes, that lines up. We'll aim for final signoff by 2025-08-08 if runs go smooth.

[06:26] Mina: A few pragmatic notes that often trip POCs: tokenization differences between SDKs, quantization-induced quality drift, and cache warmup effects. We'll include controlled runs: 1) cold start, 2) warm cache, 3) sustained concurrency.
[06:42] Priya: For the quality gating, will you show per-prompt variance? Some prompts are brittle.
[06:46] Mina: We'll include per-prompt and per-cluster breakdowns — and a top-50 failure list for manual review.

[06:55] Tom: Any license or data retention gotchas for the logs? We need logs retained for 90 days searchable for audit.
[07:02] Jordan: Redwood Console supports retention policies, and we can set 90-day retention for the POC logs. We'll include audit log config in the runbook.

[07:10] Raj: One more: competitor callouts — we ran a quick bench against Anthropic open endpoint earlier and saw slightly lower latency but higher cost. We may want to include a competitor column in the final report for context.
[07:21] Jordan: We can include a competitor baseline column if you provide the runs or let us run a quick comparative pass — we will mark it as "informational" not part of pass/fail.

[07:30] Priya: On remediation: who does the tuning? Our ML team or Redwood?
[07:34] Mina: We typically do joint troubleshooting sessions. For prompt engineering and config changes we can propose changes and run them; you can accept or run them internally. We'll document every change.

[07:42] Jordan: Ok let's capture explicit acceptance criteria in the spreadsheet and sign it off. Priya, Raj — can you confirm by end of week?
[07:49] Priya: Yes, I'll review and confirm.
[07:51] Raj: Confirmed, we'll look at the spreadsheet and get back.

[07:55] Jordan: Quick recap of next steps for the transcript: 1) Mina shares benchmark script + pass/fail spreadsheet (due 2025-07-18). 2) Priya shares eval set and traffic profile (due 2025-07-21). 3) Jordan shares security docs and pricing scenarios (due 2025-07-16). 4) Schedule infra deep-dive (2025-07-22).
[08:22] Priya: Sounds good — also can you send a short template for the manual review sample to our security team?
[08:28] Mina: Will do — sample template included in the POC_benchmarks.xlsx under the "manual_review" tab.

[08:35] Tom: One last question around metrics: for p95 latency, do you measure end-to-end (client network + service) or server-side only?
[08:42] Mina: We'll report both. Server-side latencies are the gating numbers but we'll also capture end-to-end to show real user impact.

[08:50] Jordan: Great. Unless there are any blockers, we'll wrap. Thanks everyone.
[08:55] Priya: Thanks.
[08:56] Raj: Thanks all.
